name: Faraquet
label: Dischord
lede: Three friends, a handful of singles, one album full of odd meters and melody, and a band that played so few shows that its comeback sold out Tokyo twice.

eras.title: The side project that outlived its host
eras.text: Devin Ocampo and Chad Molter had been playing together since they were about eighteen. In DC, Ocampo landed behind the drum kit in Smart Went Crazy, met Jeff Boswell there, and started something on the side that turned out to be the main event.

years.h: Faraquet starts out of Smart Went Crazy
years.p: [[Devin Ocampo|10bc183b-b6a8-4769-9e7a-0637d0f8a7a8]] switches to guitar and vocals, [[Chad Molter|794c2243-0136-4627-887c-00749b81475d]] plays drums and Jeff Boswell moves to bass; Dischord dates the start to June 1997. When [[Smart Went Crazy|d9c78028-a30b-470b-b964-2f85cab51cc2]] folds, Faraquet goes full-time.
years.xp:
Devin Ocampo and Chad Molter were old friends who moved to Washington to make music; it was [[Travis Morrison|b9ba9319-c5c7-4316-b32a-d3f92a673e1f]] of [[The Dismemberment Plan|1131e5da-dfdf-46c9-b6ff-b7ac552c2a3c]] who connected Ocampo with Smart Went Crazy, where he drummed and met Jeff Boswell.

The influences were not the usual DC ones: [[King Crimson|b38225b8-8e5f-42aa-bcdc-7bae5b5bdab3]] and Yes alongside [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]] People called it math rock. Ocampo thought that was just a simple term.

years.p: Faraquet's first single, on Mis En Scene. Dischord later gathers it onto Anthology 1997–98.

eras.title: One tower, then silence
eras.text: Two more singles, a tour with Fugazi, and The View From This Tower, cut with J. Robbins at Inner Ear. Then, with barely a run of shows behind them, Devin Ocampo, Chad Molter and Jeff Boswell decided they were done.

years.h: Faraquet's The Whole Thing Over / Call It Sane
years.p: A Faraquet 7" on DeSoto Records, plus a split with [[Akarso|5c6a66e2-d8d7-46a1-a1f2-b19f9fea2c85]] on 404 Records.

years.h: Live at the Black Cat Backstage, November 28, 1999
yt: Live at the Black Cat Backstage, November 28, 1999

years.p: Dischord's history says [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] invited Faraquet on tour, and after it Faraquet went into the studio for its first album, The View From This Tower.

years.h: The View From This Tower · Dischord No. 122
years.p: Faraquet's only studio album: nine songs recorded at Inner Ear with [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] co-producing. Cut Self Not, Carefully Planned, Study in Complacency: tight, angular, and oddly tuneful.

years.h: Faraquet breaks up at a creative standstill
years.p: Faraquet breaks up. Devin Ocampo later said they'd reached a standstill and it felt like the end of things.
years.xp:
Faraquet had existed for about four years, released one album and, by Ocampo's own account, played very few shows. There was no blowup on the record, just a band that had run out of road together.

Ocampo and Chad Molter kept going as [[Medications|c545a7bf-c8d7-4368-8009-22e19d8911ce]], which made an EP and two albums for Dischord. Ocampo went on to work as an engineer and producer at Inner Ear.

eras.title: Brazil, then home
eras.text: Fans kept asking for Faraquet's out-of-print singles. Gathering them up became an excuse to play again, starting a very long way from D.C., in Brazil.

years.p: Announced in summer 2007, Dischord No. 159 gathers Faraquet's singles and splits plus one unreleased song and one outtake, remixed by Devin Ocampo. The LP comes on opaque yellow vinyl.
years.xp: Ten songs in all, mastered by [[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] at Silver Sonya.

years.h: Faraquet's original three play D.C. again
years.p: After Devin Ocampo and Chad Molter played Brazil without Jeff Boswell in September 2007, all three reunite in Washington to mark Anthology 1997–98, as promised.

eras.title: Seventeen years later
eras.text: In the long quiet, Devin Ocampo made records with the Effects and Chad Molter launched Whisper States. Then Ocampo, Molter and Jeff Boswell booked a Faraquet tour, and most of the dates sold out.

years.h: Faraquet returns: Black Cat, then two sold-out Philadelphia sets
years.p: Faraquet announced its first shows in 17 years in April. The run opens at D.C.'s Black Cat on July 25, then sells out an early and a late show at Philadelphia's Phila MOCA before TV Eye in Ridgewood, Queens.
years.xp: [[SAVAK|798aac2b-e30f-457a-a082-2826d8a5c533]] supported on the July Mid-Atlantic dates. Cut Self Not was in the Black Cat set.

years.h: Faraquet plays Los Angeles and six nights in Japan
years.p: Faraquet sells out Zebulon in Los Angeles, then plays Tokyo, Nara, Osaka and Nagoya, with two sold-out nights at Tokyo's Fever to close.
